module purpose: neorv32_sdi takes bus writes into a control register (an enable bit and five interrupt-enable bits) and into an 8-bit transmit FIFO, synchronizes the three serial inputs sdi_clk_i, sdi_csn_i and sdi_dat_i, and runs a serial engine that, while enabled and with sdi_csn_i low, loads a byte from the transmit FIFO into a shift register, shifts sampled sdi_dat_i bits in on each detected sdi_clk_i edge while driving the register's top bit on sdi_dat_o, and after eight bits writes the assembled byte into a receive FIFO. Bus reads return the control bits, FIFO and chip-select status or the received byte, and irq_o is raised when the interface is enabled and an enabled FIFO condition holds.

use-case flows.value: control settings (enable bit and five interrupt-enable bits) taken from bus write data at the control address
transmit byte pushed from bus write data into the transmit FIFO
transfer start: with the engine enabled and chip-select low, the transmit FIFO is popped and its byte (or zero when it is empty) is loaded into the shift register

serial bit transfer: each detected serial clock edge advances the bit count and shifts the sampled data bit into the shift register, whose top bit drives sdi_dat_o; chip-select high returns the engine to idle
byte completion: after the eighth bit a done pulse writes the assembled byte into the receive FIFO
interrupt request formed from the enable bit, the interrupt-enable bits and the FIFO status outputs
control bits, FIFO status and chip-select status, or the received byte (popping the receive FIFO), returned on bus reads
control bits, interrupt, synchronizer and engine registers cleared while rstn_i is low; both FIFOs cleared while the enable bit is 0

conceptual assets.concept: Interface enable setting -- whether the serial engine may leave idle, whether both FIFOs keep their contents, and whether the interrupt can be raised
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores the bit with `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` (line 133) only under bus_req_i.stb = '1', bus_req_i.rw = '1' and bus_req_i.addr(2) = '0' (lines 130-132), and reset clears it (line 117). This entity uses the stored value: `serial.state(2) <= ctrl.enable;` (line 296) decides whether the case at line 297 can reach the load, sample and shift arms or falls to the others arm (line 338); `tx_fifo.clear <= not ctrl.enable;` (line 200) and line 239 flush both FIFOs while it is 0; and `irq_o <= ctrl.enable and (` (line 249) forces the interrupt low. A corrupted value would run or stop transfers, discard queued bytes or mask the interrupt contrary to the written setting, so Integrity is Established; Availability also holds, since transfers and FIFO contents persist only while it stays 1. ctrl.enable stores it (occurrence 3, CLOCKED_BY clk_i, line 133) and its own records show use (GATES irq_o at occurrence 7, line 249; CARRIES bus_rsp_o.data at line 143). bus_req_i and bus_rsp_o carry complete bus transactions (address, data, byte enables, strobe, read/write; acknowledge, error, read data), so they are transport and give no setting input or readback exit. tx_fifo.clear and rx_fifo.clear only pass the inverted bit to the FIFO sub-units' clear_i (lines 186, 221): carriers. serial.state bit 2 is listed under the sequencing concept.

conceptual assets.reasoning: The byte enters the transmit FIFO through `tx_fifo.wdata <= bus_req_i.data(7 downto 0);` (line 201), is loaded by `serial.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata;` (line 305) when tx_fifo.avail is not '0' (line 302), is shifted by line 327 and leaves through `sdi_dat_o <= serial.sreg(serial.sreg'left);` (line 345).
